title: Homologous Series
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
objective: Methane, ethane, propane, butane: four different compounds, one family. How each member differs from the next by one CH₂ unit, and what that means for their properties.

fill.q: Successive members of a homologous series differ by ____.
Each member of a homologous series is called a ____.
The general formula of the alkanes is ____.
Successive homologues differ in molar mass by ____ u.
Members of a homologous series have the same ____ group.

tf.q: Members of a homologous series have identical chemical properties.
The boiling point of straight-chain alkanes rises as the chain gets longer.
CH₄ and C₂H₄ belong to the same homologous series.
tf.explain: C₂H₄ is an alkene (CₙH₂ₙ); they differ by C, not CH₂.

tf.q: Methanol and propan-1-ol belong to the same homologous series.
tf.explain: Both are alcohols and differ by 2 CH₂.

ar.a: Ethane and propane are members of the same homologous series.
ar.r: They have the same general formula and differ by one CH₂ unit.

ar.a: Butane has a higher boiling point than ethane.
ar.r: Members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties.
ar.explain: Both true; R does not explain A: the larger molecule attracts its neighbours more strongly.

mcq.q: The next member after C₂H₅OH in its series is:
Members of a homologous series show a gradual change in:

mcq.explain: Same group, differ by one CH₂.

num.q: Find the molar mass of the fifth member of the alkane series (C = 12, H = 1).
How many CH₂ units separate CH₃OH and C₄H₉OH?

short.q: Write the formulas of the first four alkanes and show the common difference.
short.solution: CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀; each differs from the next by CH₂ (14 u)

match.explain: Each feature matches its consequence or formula.
